overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely create and approve executive session minutes, a backlog reaching back to 2018; the AG declined to review the notes sufficiency and redaction concerns.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to timely create and approve executive session minutes, the primary concern of the complaint.
Complainant challenged the sufficiency of meeting notes provided in response to a records request and the redactions made to them.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review whether the Committee’s notes are sufficient or whether the notes were properly redacted.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 30 days of the letter, approve all past executive session minutes that have been created but not yet approved.
Within 90 days of the letter, create and approve the remainder of the outstanding executive session minutes.
Certify in writing to the AG's office that each portion of the order on creating and approving minutes has been complied with.
No training ordered; the AG cautioned that a future similar violation may result in an intentional-violation finding and a civil penalty of up to $1,000.
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Committee, within 30 days of the date of this letter, to approve all past executive session minutes that have been created but not yet approved.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
